Taper and stem profiles

Source: vignettes/taper-profiles.Rmd
taper-profiles.Rmd

Stem functions accept measurement vectors and equation identifiers. Default diameters use inches, heights use feet, and volumes use cubic feet. units = 'metric' requires centimeters and meters and returns cubic meters.

step uses diameter units: inches for imperial calls and centimeters for metric calls.

Materialize a profile 

## Select a shipped tree
tree <- example_trees %>%
  filter(tree == 5)
tree spcd species dbh ht model
5 202 Douglas-fir 20 100 F00FW2W202 
## Calculate a stem profile
profile <- stem_profile(dbh = tree$dbh,
                        ht = tree$ht,
                        model = tree$model,
                        id = tree$tree,
                        step = 10,
                        status = TRUE)
id h dib dob cum_volume_ib cum_volume_ob status
5 1.000 21.085 23.711 0.000 0.000 0
5 1.833 19.914 22.244 1.912 2.388 0
5 2.667 19.160 21.293 3.689 4.536 0
5 3.500 18.621 20.610 5.395 6.528 0
5 4.333 18.215 20.090 7.057 8.408 0
5 5.167 17.896 19.678 8.658 10.204 0 
## Draw the modeled profile
plot(profile)

The profile contains inside- and outside-bark diameters and cumulative volumes from its lower bound. status is always present. status = TRUE suppresses row warnings. Unsupported outside-bark quantities remain missing.

Diameters and heights 

## Estimate diameter on both bark bases
diameters <- example_trees %>%
  transmute(tree,
            inside = dib(dbh = dbh, ht = ht, h = 20, model = model),
            outside = dob(dbh = dbh, ht = ht, h = 20, model = model))
tree inside outside
1 8.560 9.109
2 11.002 11.640
3 12.195 13.019
4 14.743 15.584
5 15.638 16.757
6 20.140 21.282 
## Find heights at the specified diameters
heights <- example_trees %>%
  transmute(tree,
            inside = height_at_dib(dbh = dbh, ht = ht, dib = 6, model = model),
            outside = height_at_dob(dbh = dbh, ht = ht, dob = 6, model = model))
tree inside outside
1 34.120 35.872
2 44.117 45.662
3 55.598 57.263
4 64.505 66.249
5 76.723 78.342
6 94.939 97.008

The inverse functions return the highest crossing. Additional crossings produce a diagnosis with the retained height.

Equations and registry 

## List equations for the example species
models <- taper_models(species = tree$spcd)
id family has_dob has_inverse has_integral
100FW2W202 flewelling_2pt TRUE FALSE TRUE
100JB2W202 r1_taper FALSE TRUE TRUE
200CZ2W202 r2_taper FALSE TRUE TRUE
200CZ3W202 r2_taper FALSE TRUE TRUE
200FW2W202 flewelling_2pt TRUE FALSE TRUE
300FW2W202 flewelling_2pt TRUE FALSE TRUE 
## Inspect the selected equation and its capabilities
get_taper_model(id = tree$model)
#> <taper_model F00FW2W202>
#>   family: flewelling_2pt
#>   kernel: compiled
#>   units: imperial
#>   oracle verified: yes
#>   capabilities: dob, integral

## Check the equation's available operations
capabilities <- model_capabilities(id = tree$model)
id has_dob has_inverse has_integral
F00FW2W202 TRUE FALSE TRUE 
## Check availability and the species assignment
has_taper_model(id = tree$model)
#> [1] TRUE

## Validate the equation mapping
check_taper_models(id = tree$model, spcd = tree$spcd)
#> [1] row     id      code    problem input  
#> <0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)

Source equations support package and source compatibility modes. fit_taper() estimates coefficients for session registration.
